:::{#exm-double-well-divergence}
#### Divergent starts on the double-well function for three step lengths

```{r}
#| label: double-well-divergence-r
#| echo: false
dwd_steps_pe <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1)
dwd_ratio_pe <- 1 / (2 * dwd_steps_pe)
dwd_square_pe <- 1 + dwd_ratio_pe
dwd_cut_pe <- sqrt(dwd_square_pe)
dwd_cut_round_pe <- round(dwd_cut_pe, 2)
```

For $f(x) = x^4 - 2x^2$,
@prp-double-well-divergence says that
[gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent)
[diverges to $\infty$](algebra.qmd#def-diverges-to-infinity)
from every start with
$\abs{\iterpoint{x}{0}}$ above $\sqrt{1 + 1 / (2\steplen)}$.
This [bound](sets.qmd#def-bound) is
$`{r} dwd_cut_round_pe[1]`$ for $\steplen = `{r} dwd_steps_pe[1]`$,
$`{r} dwd_cut_round_pe[2]`$ for $\steplen = `{r} dwd_steps_pe[2]`$,
and $`{r} dwd_cut_round_pe[3]`$ for $\steplen = `{r} dwd_steps_pe[3]`$.
The [second derivative](calculus.qmd#def-second-derivative) $12x^2 - 4$ is unbounded,
and by @prp-double-well-divergence every fixed [step length](#def-gradient-descent)
fails to [converge](#def-vector-sequence-limit) from some starts.
A larger step length lowers the bound,
so more starts are guaranteed to diverge.
By @cor-double-well-basin-bound,
each [basin of attraction](#def-basin-of-attraction) lies within the same
[bounded](algebra.qmd#def-bounded) [interval](sets.qmd#def-interval),
which narrows as $\steplen$ grows.
In the earlier [basin example](#exm-basin-of-attraction),
$\steplen = 0.05$,
and the start $4$ lies above the bound $`{r} dwd_cut_round_pe[2]`$,
which is why its [iterates](#def-iterate) grow.

:::
